CONTRACT v3: only `title` (≤6 words), `value`/figures, `note` (≤140 chars, partner-clean plain English), `status` (enum: market_priced | modeled | upside), and `fn` (footnote key) render — plus verbatim copy fields (headline/subline/lead/body/chips/cards). Underscore-prefixed fields NEVER reach the DOM. null/missing = render nothing. Footnotes render ONCE in a single 'Notes & assumptions' section above the contact form; a footnote's source_url may render as a small domain chip, never as a naked URL in body copy. Never render: held corridors (Coronado Ferry Landing, National City, Barrio Logan), Gulf counterparties, authority contacts, internal dock-status fields, naval installations (navy_honesty gate). SAN DIEGO FRAME: single-landlord market — the Port of San Diego holds the tidelands under every landing; one authority can enable the entire network. Enable-dominant; local 'Operate' energy is fund/contract on private operators (Coronado fare-free runs since 1993; CARB $15.27M e-ferry grant).

copy.framing: Two ways to partner — a genuine choice. San Diego is a single-landlord market: one authority holds the tidelands under every landing on this network, so one relationship can enable the whole map.
copy.enable_track: Grant berth access at existing piers and marinas and a permitting pathway for a pilot corridor. Private capital finances the fleet; employer demand fills the seats. The ask is access, not money — and one Board can enable the entire network.
copy.operate_track: No public body operates ferries on this bay — public money here funds service on private operators. A member city has bought down commuter fares since 1993, and the state has funded electric vessels. Navier service can be contracted the same way.

copy.headline: Your speed rules were written for boats that make wake.
copy.framing: The bay's numeric speed pockets protect mooring fields and shallow, wildlife-adjacent water. A foiling, electric Navier answers the wake purpose inherently — and respects the wildlife purpose where low wake is not the point.
copy.ask: Our ask: measure us. Where independent wake and noise measurement shows a rule's purpose is served, grant route-specific relief through mechanisms the Port Code already contains.
chips: Relief ✓ in the Port's own code

expander.title: What the Port's own code already allows
body: San Diego Bay's numeric speed rules are Port ordinances with their own relief geometry built in. The South Bay 5 mph rule exempts vessels transiting the marked Chula Vista Harbor Channel seaward of daymarks 11 and 12 — there, the code's own reasonable-and-prudent standard governs, not a numeric cap (Port Code §4.30(c)3).

Base schedule math on this network keeps the posted 5 mph tail everywhere. If the Port confirms that foilborne transit of the marked channel qualifies as prudent speed, South Bay trips get meaningfully shorter — the Port's own code text already provides for it.
Glorietta Bay's 5 mph rule (§4.35(c)3) protects a mooring field from wake — a purpose a foiling vessel serves inherently. A measured-wake case to the Port is the honest path there.
Precedent: Stockholm's public transport authority runs an electric hydrofoil ferry at roughly twice the posted zone speed under a low-wake exemption.

rule_basis.detail: reasonable-and-prudent standard; no general numeric limit in the main channel
South Bay 5 mph except while transiting the marked Chula Vista Harbor Channel seaward of daymarks 11 and 12, where §4.04 governs
5 mph in Glorietta Bay, the Bay Bridge Mooring Area, and the Central San Diego Bay Anchorage
5 mph within 200 ft of passenger landing floats — governs every berth approach; defers to local rules

_provenance.honest_split: Per SPEED-RULES §4: Glorietta Bay / anchorage pockets are wake-purpose rules a foiling N45 serves inherently; the South Bay 5 mph area is shallow-water/wildlife-purpose (USFWS refuge: sea turtles, eelgrass, nesting terns/plovers) — the relief case there is honest only inside the marked channel, where the code already switches to prudent speed. The ~15–25 min/leg extreme estimate stays internal until a written Harbor Police/Port reading exists; rendered copy says 'materially' with the pending caveat.
_provenance.rulemaker: Board of Port Commissioners (ordinance), enforced by San Diego Harbor Police. Federal instruments are routing/authorization constraints, not speed-relief candidates — never rendered (navy_honesty gate).

navier_intro.title: Meet the vessel

copy.headline: Zero-emission. Near-silent. Almost no wake.
copy.subline: Navier is a U.S. builder of electric hydrofoil vessels — the traits that matter for bay rules and bayfront neighbors are built into the hull, not bolted on.
copy.body: The N45 Explorer carries 30 passengers at a foilborne cruise speed of about 30 knots, lifted clear of the water for a smooth, wake-free ride. The smaller N30 Quanta carries 8. Foiling cuts energy use by up to ~90% versus a conventional planing hull, and both vessels run near-silent on electric power.

reference.title: Reference

copy.intro: San Diego Bay's water-transportation landscape is unusually simple: one authority manages the tidelands under every landing on this network. We seek conversations — nothing here implies approval, endorsement, or commitment by any body named.

bodies.body: Port of San Diego (San Diego Unified Port District)
bodies.role: Holds the tidelands trust for 34 miles of waterfront across five member cities — landlord for every landing on this network, vessel regulator via the Port Code, and planner via the Port Master Plan.
Certifies the Port Master Plan and its amendments; master-plan-level changes at landings route through its certification. Existing landings used as-is generally do not.
Statutory oversight of the granted public-trust lands; the trust purposes — commerce, navigation, fisheries, recreation — are the legal spine of any water-transit case.
The region's planning organization; its 2025 Regional Plan funds transit expansion. No published water-transit program — an engagement conversation, not a citation.
Runs the region's bus and Trolley network — the Blue Line links Chula Vista and downtown. Relevance is modal integration at the piers, not water operations.
State funder of zero-emission vessels — $15.27M already awarded toward two fully electric 275-passenger ferries on this bay.
City jurisdiction landside of the Embarcadero; its Climate Action Plan targets 25% walking, 10% cycling, and 15% transit mode share by 2035.
Port partner on the Chula Vista Bayfront Master Plan — Gaylord Pacific, Sweetwater Park, Harbor Park — and a vocal champion of water service to its bayfront.
Has funded fare-free weekday commuter ferry runs on this bay since 1993 — the market's clearest precedent for publicly funded water commuting.

bodies.body: U.S. Coast Guard Sector San Diego (Captain of the Port)
bodies.role: Federal navigation authorization and enforcement on the bay; a scheduled service briefs the Captain of the Port early as routine practice.

bodies.body: U.S. Fish & Wildlife Service — San Diego Bay National Wildlife Refuge
bodies.role: Steward of the South Bay refuge — eelgrass beds, mudflats, sea turtles, nesting shorebirds. A consultation stakeholder for any South Bay schedule case.
